Critically, the paper does not report whole-brain between-group voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) as coordinate tables or explicit voxelwise contrasts suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis (I6 and I7 not met; I8 not satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the paper cannot be included for a coordinate-based meta-analysis targeting bvFTD voxelwise results.

The full text presents whole-brain VBM-style analyses and reports group-level voxelwise atrophy maps and peak voxels (Table 3) for autopsy-confirmed FTD subgroups, but it does not explicitly state inclusion of patients clinically diagnosed with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM-style voxelwise structural MRI analyses), I5 (≥6 participants present in a group — 12 healthy controls in imaging subgroup), I6 (reports peak voxels/locations in Table 3), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with correction), I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no explicit identification of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered by the full text. Note: imaging subgroup patient counts per pathology subgroup are small (tau-positive n=5, tau-negative n=4, fv-AD n=3), which further limits applicability to bvFTD-specific contrasts. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: E3 applied (study reports regional lobar volumetry only; no voxelwise whole-brain/voxel-level results). Inclusion met: I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD subgroup using Neary criteria), I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=12, semantic dementia n=13, controls n=24). Inclusion not met: I3 (imaging modality is volumetric MRI segmentation, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group results reported in stereotactic coordinates [MNI/Talairach]), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because the imaging modality and reporting format do not meet required voxelwise/coordinate-based whole-brain criteria, and the paper provides only regional volumetric (ROI/lobar) analyses.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise atrophy findings with adequate sample sizes (FTLD N=18, controls N=40), but the abstract does not specify that the FTLD group corresponds to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD), nor does it report stereotactic coordinates or the reference space (MNI/Talairach). Unable to verify key inclusion criteria from the missing full text. Therefore excluded due to incomplete full text and inability to confirm I4 and I6 (and I8 where applicable).

This multicenter empirical study uses 18F-FDG PET (I3) and includes a large frontal-variant FTD sample (described as “frontal variant” FTD, equivalent to bvFTD) meeting the bvFTD criterion (I4). Sample sizes exceed the threshold (98 FTD; I5). The analysis includes voxel-wise, whole-brain comparisons normalized to the Talairach and Tournoux atlas with voxel-by-voxel Z maps and 3D-SSP displays, fulfilling reporting of between-group voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space (I6) and providing group-level whole-brain voxelwise results clearly tied to the target clinical groups (I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and supplemental materials, consistent with reporting allowance (I8). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria were met.

This is an empirical structural MRI volumetry study of FTLD subtypes (FTD, FTD/SD, PNFA) with 22 patients (17 scanned) and comparison subjects, using a region-based SABRE segmentation and multivariate PLS relating regional volumes to autobiographical memory. Inclusion met: I4 (patients diagnosed as FTD per Neary et al., which corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD) and I5 (sample sizes >6). Exclusion met: E3. The study does NOT meet I3 because the imaging modality is structural ROI-based volumetry (SABRE) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. It does NOT meet I6 because no results are reported as between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach coordinate space, and it does NOT meet I7 because it does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts (analyses are region-based and multivariate rather than voxelwise with coordinate tables). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing required imaging and whole-brain/coordinate reporting criteria (I3, I6, I7).

This is an empirical VBM study with whole-brain voxelwise analyses linking gray matter loss to behavioral profiles in a clinical FTD sample. Imaging modality: VBM (meets I3). Sample: 62 clinically diagnosed FTD patients, of whom 48 are described as behavioral-presentation (bvFTD) (meets I4). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (meets I5). Results include between-group patient vs. control contrasts and voxelwise correlational analyses reported with Talairach coordinates and whole-brain FWE-corrected findings (meets I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not a review; not ROI-only; not restricted to other modalities; no indication of comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia/susbtance history issues). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clearly clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD sample (51 bv-FTD patients) (I4); sample sizes exceed the minimum (51 patients, 14 controls) (I5); reports voxelwise group-level VBM contrasts and regional results with cluster information, BA labels, and reference to coordinate tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, voxelwise imaging analyses with multiple-comparisons thresholds, results, and discussion; supplementary coordinate tables are referenced. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis; not ROI-only; not non-empirical; not an excluded modality). Full text appears to contain core article content (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a VBM study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons between mutation carrier groups and controls and includes analyses restricted to clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects (n=7 PGRN, n=11 MAPT). Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The paper includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and a bvFTD-only analysis (I4). Sample sizes meet the threshold (≥6 in patient subgroups; I5). Whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported and illustrated (figures) and coordinate results are referenced in supplementary table e-1 (satisfying I6, I7); supplementary results are acceptable per I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not methods-only, and not a prohibited modality). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD subgroup n=15 tau-positive, n=30 TDP-43-positive; controls n=35) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (figures and slice renders). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (MNI or Talairach) for between-group contrasts nor specify that results are listed in a standard stereotactic space; the methods describe normalization to a customized template, and results are presented as figures without coordinate tables in the supplied content. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (reporting at least one between-group contrast result in a defined stereotactic space) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply based on the provided content. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This full-text reports an empirical FDG-PET study that includes a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant frontotemporal dementia (fv-FTD) group (n=18), which corresponds to behavioral variant FTD. The paper uses resting-state FDG-PET and SPM voxelwise analyses (whole-brain) and reports correlations/localizations using Talairach/MNI-based atlases. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the target patient group are presented (tables/figures described). The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8, and it does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric analyses from structural MRI (T1-weighted regional VOIs) and does not provide any whole-brain, voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates. Exclusion met: E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (sample size criterion satisfied: 21 FTD patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural ROI volumetry, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I4 (paper reports ‘FTD’ but does not specifically confirm clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach or Talairach space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (no whole-brain results or coordinate tables/figures). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (66 bvFTD, 30 controls). The methods state voxel-based morphometry was performed in SPM5 with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons (FWE-corrected) between bvFTD subtypes and controls; results are reported in figures/tables describing regional atrophy. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The paper provides full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and reports whole-brain group contrasts in stereotactic space using standard VBM workflows. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (typical AD, atypical AD, FTLD, controls) with conjunction and direct contrasts. It includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among its sampled clinical subgroups (bvFTD n=3 within atypical AD and bvFTD n=3 within FTLD), and has adequate sample sizes in disease groups (FTLD n=14) and controls (n=20), meeting the minimum sample-size requirement. Whole-brain VBM results are described in the Results (with voxelwise contrasts and conjunction analyses), and ROI/parcellation analyses are also reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, uses VBM not excluded modalities). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Exclusion IDs met: none.
Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (sample sizes ≥6: bvFTD n=11; total patients n=32; controls n=24).
Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (study uses volumetric MRI BBSI/VBSI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise results reported in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise/coordinate-based results from the target sample). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet key imaging and reporting inclusion criteria required by the review and is excluded.

Although this paper meets all imaging and reporting inclusion criteria (resting-state fMRI ICA; clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; sample sizes n=12 per group; reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts with MNI-style coordinates and figures/tables), it includes 3 bvFTD patients with comorbid motor neuron disease (documented in the Methods/Subjects section). This constitutes concurrent neurological symptoms in the sample, which violates exclusion criterion E4. Therefore the study is excluded. All other inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are satisfied; no other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This FDG-PET study includes 7 frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients and reports whole-brain SPM results in MNI space (I3, I5, I6, I7, I8 met). However, the manuscript does not specify that the FTD patients are the behavioral variant (bvFTD) required by the review objective. Because inclusion criterion I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD) is not satisfied / cannot be confirmed from the full text, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This VBM study meets several inclusion criteria (I3: uses voxel-based morphometry; I4: sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within pathologic subgroups; I5: sample sizes meet the ≥6 requirement [28 patients, 50 controls]). However it fails key required items: I7 is not met because the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result that is clearly identified as coming specifically from the target clinical group (bvFTD); whole-brain results are reported for pathologic TDP-43 subtypes (type 1/2/3), not for a bvFTD clinical subgroup. I6 is not met based on the provided full text because no between-group contrast coordinates (MNI or Talairach) or explicit coordinate tables are presented here; results are described and shown as thresholded maps but coordinates are not provided in the supplied content. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically defined frontal-variant FTLD group fulfilling bvFTD criteria (fvFTLD; I4) with n=19 (I5). Voxelwise SPMs and regional maxima are reported and coordinates are described in MNI space/supplementary material (I8). However, the paper does not report any between-group VBM contrasts (patient vs control) or other between-group voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space, so it fails inclusion criterion I6. Additionally, although subgroup voxelwise analyses were performed for the fvFTLD (bvFTD) subgroup, these yielded no significant whole-brain voxelwise findings; the positive voxelwise results reported derive from the combined FTLD group rather than from the bvFTD subgroup specifically, so the study does not meet I7 (group-level whole-brain result clearly from the target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I6 and I7.

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study that includes a behavioural-variant FTD subgroup (10 bvFTD patients). Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) using SPM/DARTEL (I3). Sample: includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=10) and healthy controls; subgroup size >6 (I4, I5). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain VBM results for the combined FTLD group, syndromic subgroups, and a between-group VBM comparison of FTLD versus healthy controls (voxel-wise maps with thresholds, cluster reporting), fulfilling whole-brain, voxelwise reporting for the target sample (I6, I7). Results are presented as statistical parametric maps and summary tables/figures (coordinates/voxelwise results stated to be reported/displayed), acceptable per criteria (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain analyses present; not a review; not ROI-only; not an excluded modality). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it uses manual ROI structural MRI volumetry of the hypothalamus (and postmortem tissue analyses) rather than VBM, task or resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET, so it does not meet the required imaging modality (I3). It does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and has adequate sample size (18 bvFTD patients and 16 controls; I5). However, the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise whole-brain contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and does not provide whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Because it reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results, it meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED.

This study should be excluded because it does not clearly include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients, and it does not report between-group voxelwise contrast coordinates in a standardized stereotactic space from the study sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used) and I5 (sample sizes: 14 FTLD patients and 13 controls; both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (bvFTD diagnosis not specified; sample described as FTLD without subtype specification), I6 (no explicit between-group contrast coordinates in MNI/Talairach reported for this sample), and I7 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result with coordinates attributable to the target sample in the required stereotactic space). Exclusion criteria violated: none (E2,E3,E4,E5,E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on volumetric MRI (SPM5) to compare 15 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (5 PiD, 5 CBD, 5 FTLD-TDP type 1) to 20 controls. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (including peak voxel coordinates in Table 3) and direct between-group contrasts, satisfying the requirement for results in a defined stereotactic space. Sample sizes meet the >=6 participant criterion for patient and control groups. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain analyses, not only ROI, not an excluded modality). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (VBM was performed), I4 (sample includes FTD patients meeting Neary criteria consistent with behavioral-variant FTD), I5 (group sizes meet the minimum: FTD n=11 overall; VBM subset includes 6 FTD). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (the study does not report a between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space comparing bvFTD vs controls; VBM results are reported as voxelwise regression correlations across pooled subjects rather than between-group contrasts), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result is clearly identified as coming from the target sample group—i.e., a bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast is not presented). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This full-text reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses using Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (and TBSS/DTI) and presents group-level contrasts in standard space (MNI). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=13) with age-matched healthy controls, meeting the minimum sample size requirement. The paper provides whole-brain, voxelwise results (VBM and TBSS) displayed in figures and supplementary tables (coordinate-based results consistent with MNI space). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and statistical thresholds), Results, and Discussion, so core article content is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis focusing on bvFTD imaging studies.

The study is excluded because its imaging analysis is cortical thickness derived from structural MRI (surface-based cortical thickness), which does not meet the required imaging modalities (I3: VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and matches exclusion criterion E6 (studies that only report cortical thickness methods). The paper does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD; n=17), I5 (sample sizes ≥6 in patient and control groups), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise contrasts using SPM5 and reports cortical thinning clusters), and I7 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded due to E6.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports MNI-space results, and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (some C9ORF72 cases had bvFTD). However, the group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported for the genetic subgroup (C9ORF72 mutation carriers, n=11) rather than for a clinically defined bvFTD group. The review requires at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result explicitly coming from a bvFTD target sample; that is not provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7, so it must be excluded despite meeting other imaging and sample-size criteria.

Full text provided is only the abstract (fulltext_incomplete). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used voxel-based morphometry) and I4 (includes bvFTD sample) are evident from the abstract. Inclusion criteria not verifiable/met: I5 (sample size >=6 not reported in abstract), I6 (reporting of between-group contrast coordinates in MNI/Talairach not stated), I7 (clear whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results not fully documented), I8 (acceptable reporting format for whole-brain results cannot be confirmed). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met. Because critical methodological details (sample size and coordinate/whole-brain reporting) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be confidently included.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level comparisons (I3, I7). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with adequate sample size (bvFTD groups: C9+ n=15, noncarriers n=48) satisfying the minimum-6-participant requirement for patient groups (I5). Between-group contrasts are reported with Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) slice coordinates and familywise-error corrected voxelwise results (I6, I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis; not ROI-only; empirical VBM whole-brain analyses reported; does not rely solely on seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness; no disqualifying comorbid-sample issues indicated). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of bvFTD VBM studies.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) (I4), had sufficient group sizes (bvFTD=15, controls=18) (I5), conducted voxel-wise between-group contrasts in MNI standard space (I6) and reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (I7) with results presented in figures/thresholded maps overlaid on MNI (I8). The full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review/meta-analysis; not ROI-only; sample excludes comorbid psychiatric/other dementia; empirical VBM study not limited to DTI/seed FC).

This full-text task-based fMRI study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Neary/revised criteria), uses fMRI (with voxel-wise grey matter covariate/VBM preprocessing), has adequate sample size (20 patients, 18 controls), reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with stereotaxic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) and whole-brain cluster correction, and presents group-level, voxelwise results in tables/figures described in the text. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and reports voxel-wise, whole-brain SPM analyses with identified clusters/coordinates linking hypometabolism to theory-of-mind deficits. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 requirement. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM8, MNI normalization) reported in tables/figures and describes clusters surviving correction. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review, only other modalities, comorbid psychiatric/substance issues) are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and neuroimaging tables/figures; thus full text appears complete.

This VBM study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (12 bvFTD), uses VBM (I3), has adequate sample sizes (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space including a subgroup analysis restricted to bvFTD (I4, I7, I8). However, it does not report any between-group contrast (e.g., patients vs controls) in stereotactic space; the neuroimaging findings are voxelwise correlations of grey matter with behavioural scores within the patient cohort and subgroup, not between-group comparisons. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (at least one result of a between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I6 is not satisfied. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I6. Exclusion IDs met: none ([]).

This is an original empirical resting-state fMRI study (also reports VBM and clinical FDG-PET data) that explicitly recruited and clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) alongside controls and probable AD patients. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=12; controls n=30). Analyses were performed in standard space (MNI) using SPM/ICA, and the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise comparisons (cluster-level FWE-corrected results) and network-level between-group contrasts. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and no exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-only/DTI/thickness-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample).

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=17), uses whole-brain VBM, reports results in MNI coordinates, and meets sample size requirements. However, all voxelwise whole-brain results are reported for the combined FTD group (mixed bvFTD, svPPA, nfvPPA) rather than for a bvFTD-only subgroup. The meta-analysis requires at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target sample (bvFTD). No bvFTD-specific whole-brain results or coordinates are provided, so inclusion criterion I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not report whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). It used resting-state fMRI (I3) in clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (I4) with adequate sample size (18 patients; I5). However, analyses were performed on 90 AAL regions and reported region-level graph/network metrics and inter-regional connectivity (ROI/parcellation-based), without voxelwise coordinate results or MNI/Talairach coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrast in defined stereotactic space) and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result) are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E3 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study (voxel-based morphometry in SPM8) that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=18) and healthy controls (n=18), meeting sample-size requirements. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (controls > FTD and controls > PSP) and VBM correlations with environmental-dependency scores, with results presented as clusters and figures/tables (methods state normalization to template space in SPM8, implying standard MNI space). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and there is no indication of excluded comorbid psychiatric/neurologic disorders. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-FC/DTI/thickness-only). Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3); includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (5 of 15; I4); has sample size >=6 (n=15 FTD; I5); reports between-group contrasts comparing FTD patients to healthy controls and identifies regions of maximal group distinction via whole-brain analyses (ROIs derived from group contrasts), consistent with reporting of group-level voxelwise results (references to eTable 1, figures and group contrasts) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6, I7). The manuscript references tables/figures/supplementary materials with the group-level results (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical original data, not seed-only/DTI/cortical thickness, and no indication of disqualifying comorbid samples). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Excluded because the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result that is clearly identified as coming from the target sample group (bvFTD). The bvFTD-versus-control findings are reported using small-volume correction / ROI-based analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results specific to bvFTD. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients included, n=12), I5 (sample size ≥6), I6 (results reported with MNI coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise group result). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI/SVC analyses for bvFTD with no bvFTD whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Although this prospective cohort includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets I4) with adequate sample sizes (10 carriers, 19 noncarriers, 35 controls; meets I5) and used FDG-PET in a subset (meets I3), the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor does it provide coordinate tables from such analyses. Imaging results are primarily MRI visual rating scales (region-based) and descriptive FDG-PET findings in individual cases. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met, and the study effectively reports only ROI/visual-rating or descriptive PET results, triggering exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22) compared to AD and controls. It uses voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) as the imaging modality, reports group-level voxelwise analyses with reported MNI coordinates, and provides whole-brain voxelwise results (within frontal/temporal mask) clearly identified for the bvFTD group. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD n=22, controls n=35). Results are reported in the main text, figures and coordinate tables. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Meets all inclusion criteria: study uses VBM (I3) in addition to DTI; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) (I4) and group sizes exceed 6 (I5). Reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with results projected to standard MNI space and FWE-corrected maps (I6, I7), with figures/tables and supporting information describing whole-brain results (I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion so is complete. No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical, original study (not a review), includes whole-brain VBM results (not ROI-only), and although it also reports DTI, it is not a DTI-only study (does not trigger E6). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4), uses Voxel-Based Morphometry alongside DTI (VBM satisfies I3), includes more than six participants per group (I5), and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses referenced to standard space (MNI) with voxelwise results shown in figures and described in the text (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, empirical data, and does not consist solely of excluded modalities). Full text appears complete, containing introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I include this study for the review focused on bvFTD imaging.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) and uses RS-fMRI and VBM (meets imaging modality). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients and controls n=15). Data were spatially normalized to Talairach space and report group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ICA-derived RSN maps, group t-maps, VBM whole-brain results), satisfying reporting of between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.
